title: Ratios and rates
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.rat.ratios.equivalent: Find what one number was multiplied by, and multiply the other number by the same.
hints.rat.ratios.unit-rate: For one, divide the total by how many. To compare deals, find the price for one in each.
hints.rat.ratios.proportion: Match the parts that go together. Find what the bottom was multiplied by, and do the same to the top.
hints.rat.ratios: Ratios grow by multiplying both numbers by the same thing. For one, divide.
hints.rat.ratios.scale: Real distances are bigger: multiply by what 1 unit stands for. Drawing lengths are smaller: divide. For a scale like 2 cm : 15 m, count how many times the scale fits.

misconceptionMessages.rat.additive: Ratios grow by multiplying, not adding: 3 : 4 doubled is 6 : 8, not 6 : 7.
misconceptionMessages.rat.ratio-swapped: Check which number goes with which: keep flour with flour and sugar with sugar.
misconceptionMessages.rat.rate-flipped: For the amount for ONE, divide the total by how many: $12 ÷ 4.
misconceptionMessages.rat.rate-multiplied: You're finding the amount for one, so the answer should be smaller: divide, don't multiply.
misconceptionMessages.rat.better-buy-total: The cheaper pack isn't always the better buy. Find the price for ONE in each pack and compare.
misconceptionMessages.rat.proportion-cross-wrong: Line up the matching parts first: top with top, bottom with bottom. Then multiply across the right way.
misconceptionMessages.rat.scale-wrong-way: Check the direction: the real thing is bigger than the drawing. Drawing to real, multiply; real to drawing, divide.
misconceptionMessages.rat.scale-ignored-first: The scale is 2 cm for 15 m, not 1 cm for 15 m. Count how many 2s fit in the drawing length, then take that many 15s.

sections.title: Equivalent ratios
sections.objective: Find a missing number in a ratio like 3 : 4 = 12 : ?.
explain: A ratio compares two amounts: 3 cups of flour for every 4 cups of sugar.
Making more batches multiplies both amounts by the same number.

visual.caption: 3 cups of flour for every 4 cups of sugar. Tap for more batches.

sections.key: Equivalent ratios come from multiplying (or dividing) both numbers by the same number. Never by adding.

sections.title: Unit rates
sections.objective: Find the amount for one: price per item, miles per hour.
explain: To compare deals, find the price for one in each and compare those.
sections.key: A unit rate is the amount for ONE. Divide the total by how many.

worked.math: 150 miles in 3 hours: 150 ÷ 3 = [[50]] miles per hour

sections.title: Proportions
explain: A proportion says two ratios are equal.
Match the parts that go together, then scale; or cross-multiply.
sections.key: Line up the matching parts. Whatever the bottom was multiplied by, multiply the top by the same.

sections.title: Scale drawings and maps
sections.objective: Use a scale like 1 inch = 20 miles or 2 cm : 15 m to go between a drawing and real life.
explain: A scale is a ratio: drawing length : real length. It stays the same everywhere on the map or plan.
Real things are bigger than their drawing, so check your answer goes the right way.

visual.caption: 1 inch for 20 miles. Tap to see 2, 3 and 5 inches.

sections.key: A scale is a ratio that stays the same. Drawing to real: multiply. Real to drawing: divide. For 2 cm : 15 m, count how many times the scale fits.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.key: Ratios grow by multiplying. For one, divide. In a proportion, match the parts and scale.

worked.math: A car goes 120 miles on 4 gallons.
